smallest_supported_cross_provider_claims: GitHub Copilot, Cursor, Replit, and Devin document isolated execution units; Factory documents persistent or disposable compute choices; Codex documents a sandbox boundary. These are not equivalent isolation contracts.
Factory, GitHub Copilot, Cursor, Replit, and Devin document parallel or delegated work, but parent-child identity, dependency, join, and conflict behavior differ.
Factory, GitHub Copilot, Cursor, Replit, and Devin expose stop, cancel, interrupt, archive, resume, checkpoint, or takeover mechanisms, but recovery semantics are not interchangeable.
All six providers expose observable lifecycle state or events; only some expose schema-constrained structured output, and none makes runtime completion semantic conformance or promotion authority.
Human review remains separate in documented flows; a successful session, green test, pushed commit, applied task, or merged PR proves a different claim.
limitations: Only official public sources were inspected.
No product was run and no proprietary behavior was inferred.
